title: To Cook Kangaroo
description: Prepared with kangaroo, onion, and peppercorns.
steps: Take the hind-quarters, above the kidney.
Cut off the tail, also the legs, at the first joint from the back.
Discard the feet and cut up the remainder of the legs with the tail to stew for gravy.
Add to the gravy meat a small onion sliced, a few peppercorns, and one or two bay leaves.
Let it stew till all goodness is out of the meat, then strain.
Make a good stuffing as for turkey, with a large cupful of grated bread, half as much shred suet, some thyme, parsley, and a small portion of onion, chopped very fine.
Add either half a pound of sausage-meat, or a little finely-shred ham or bacon.
Season with pepper and salt, and mix well with one or two eggs.
Put as much stuffing as it will hold into the aperture of the body and make the rest into balls about the size of pullets' eggs.
You may lard the kangaroo, but it is very good without, if covered with a caul of sweet mutton suet while baking.
Bake with long cooking, letting it stay in the oven a full half hour after you think it done.
Serve with some of the gravy having added to it some mushroom ketchup, and a little flour and butter.
Have currant jelly to eat with it or some persons prefer ham or bacon instead.
Hashed with the remaining gravy, the kangaroo is often nicer than it was the first day.

title: To Make Bread
description: A bread preparation made with yeast, milk or water, and flour.
steps: Put a bushel of flour into a kneading trough
Mix a pint of yeast thoroughly with as much milk-warm water
Make a deep hole in the middle of the flour, and pour the yeast and water into it
Take a spoon and work it round the edges of this body of moisture, so as to bring into it by degrees flour enough to make a thin batter
Stir well for a minute or two
Throw a handful of flour over the surface of this batter, and cover the whole with a cloth thickly folded to keep it warm
Set it by the fire, regulating the distance by the state of the weather and the season of the year

Beginning round the hole containing the batter, work the flour into it, pouring in milk-warm water or milk as it is wanted
When the whole mass is moistened, knead it well
Mould the loaves, let them rise for twenty minutes
Put them into an oven that has been previously heated
Bake for about an hour for a four pound loaf, fifty minutes for a three pound, and so on in proportion

title: To Make Strong Beer or Ale
description: Prepared with malt, hops or beer or ale, and yeast.

ingredients.name: Twelve bushels of malt to the hogshead for beer, and eight for ale
ingredients.sourceText: Twelve bushels of malt to the hogshead for beer, and eight for ale

ingredients.name: Three-quarters of a pound of hops to a bushel for strong beer, or half a pound for ale
ingredients.sourceText: Three-quarters of a pound of hops to a bushel for strong beer, or half a pound for ale

ingredients.name: A pound and a half of hops dried before the fire
ingredients.sourceText: A pound and a half of hops dried before the fire

steps: Pour the whole quantity hot, but not boiling, on at once, and let it infuse three hours, being covered
Mash it in the first half-hour, and let it stand the remainder of the time
Run it on the hops, previously infused in water
Boil them with the wort two hours from the time it begins to boil
Cool a pailful to add two quarts of yeast to, which will prepare it for putting to the rest when ready next day; but if possible, put them together the same night
Tun as usual
Cover the bung-hole with paper when the beer has done working
When it is to be stopped, have ready a pound and a half of hops dried before the fire, put them into the bung-hole, and fasten it up
After the beer or ale has run from the grains, you can make table-beer of a similar quantity

Thicken the liquor that it was stewed in with a little flour, and season with pepper, salt, anchovy, and mushroom ketchup, and chilli vinegar.
When it has boiled about ten minutes, either pour it over the fish or return the fish into the stewpan to warm.

steps: Beat and season the boned shoulder.
Supply the want of fat with that of a fine well-hung loin of mutton, steeped twenty-four hours in equal parts of rape, vinegar, and port.
Rub the shoulder well with sugar for two or three days.
Wipe it extremely clean from the sugar and the wine.
Cut the meat into pieces two inches square.
Put them into a stewpan with two gills of port wine, one of claret, a few shalots, some pepper, salt, mace, and allspice, and enough stock to cover it.
Let it simmer until three parts done.
Take out the meat you intend for the pasty, and put into a deep dish with a part of the liquor.
Cover the pasty an inch thick with paste.
Bake for two hours.

Before it is sent to table pour in a sauce made from the liquor the venison was stewed in, free from fat, with added pepper, salt, the juice of half a lemon, and half a gill of port wine or claret, and a little thickening.

steps: Mix all to a stiff paste, moistening with a little milk if necessary, but be careful, for milk will make the pudding heavy.

Instead of Noyeau three-quarters of a pint of Madeira may be used.

Spread them with the marmalade
Fit them neatly into a buttered pie-dish until it is half full
Pour over them gradually a hot custard made of the milk heated almost to boiling, then taken off the fire, and the beaten eggs and sugar stirred in with the flavoring

Grate a little nutmeg on the top

Pour over it a pint of boiled custard

title: Apples à la Princess Maude
description: Prepared with apples, lemon, and gelatine.

ingredients.name: one and a half pounds of good cooking apples
ingredients.sourceText: one and a half pounds of good cooking apples

ingredients.name: three-quarters of a pint of water
ingredients.sourceText: three-quarters of a pint of water

ingredients.name: four to six ounces of loaf sugar
ingredients.sourceText: four to six ounces of loaf sugar

ingredients.name: finely cut peel of one lemon
ingredients.sourceText: finely cut peel of one lemon

ingredients.name: three-quarters of an ounce of leaf gelatine
ingredients.sourceText: three-quarters of an ounce of leaf gelatine

steps: Peel one and a half pounds of good cooking apples, cut them up and cook them in three-quarters of a pint of water with four to six ounces of loaf sugar, according to the sweetness of the apples, and bay-leaves, and the finely cut peel of one lemon.
When the apples are perfectly soft, dissolve with them three-quarters of an ounce of leaf gelatine and pass the whole through a sieve.
Divide the puree into two parts, and redden one of them with liquid carmine, and whiten the other with a little thick cream.
Put them in separate sauce pans to about a quarter of an inch thick, and let them set on broken ice.

Cut out in rounds with a plain cutter about the size of a shilling for ornamenting round the mould, and in leaf shapes for the bottom and in the centre of each of the rounds set a little round of angelica with a little liquid jelly.
Line a plain round mould with lemon jelly to about one-eighth of an inch thick.
Set the cut leaves of apple puree regularly on the bottom of the mould with the stock ends at the centre and the rounds regularly round the sides in alternate colors.
Fix these in their places with a little more of the lemon jelly.
Separately dissolve the odds and ends of the cuttings of the puree with two tablespoonfuls of lemon jelly, and let them stand till somewhat cool.
Add to each a quarter of a pint of thickly whipped cream and pour them into the mould in alternate layers and put to set on broken ice.
When required turn out on a dish.
Place on the top a ball of stiffly whipped cream sweetened and flavored with vanilla essence, and lightly sprinkle with a little chopped pistachio nuts.

title: Baked Rice Curry
description: Prepared with rice, onion, and melted butter.
steps: Wash a cupful of raw rice in three waters, and let it soak fifteen minutes in water enough to cover it.
Boil an onion in a quart of water with a little salt until the onion is very soft.
